nodes.description: Address of the contract owner, initialized to msg.sender at deployment.
Stored keccak256 hash of the secret winning number used by guess().
Public withdraw function that checks msg.sender == owner and transfers the whole balance to owner.
Public payable guess function that compares keccak256(number) with the secret hash and pays out the jackpot.
Caller-controlled address used for access control in withdraw() and as payout recipient in guess().
External value transfer owner.transfer(this.balance) executed inside withdraw().
External value transfer msg.sender.transfer(this.balance + msg.value) executed inside guess() on a successful guess.
uint8 guess parameter hashed with keccak256 and compared against secretNumberHash.
Arithmetic expression this.balance + msg.value used as the payout amount in guess().

edges.reason: The owner state variable is read in the require(msg.sender == owner) gate that controls whether withdraw() proceeds.
msg.sender is the caller identity checked against owner, gating privileged withdrawal of the contract balance.
Execution of withdraw() leads directly to the external owner.transfer(this.balance) call.
The owner address determines the recipient of the full contract balance in the external transfer.
secretNumberHash is read and compared against keccak256(number) inside guess().
msg.sender funds and receives from guess(); the caller and msg.value drive the jackpot condition and payout.
The number parameter controls the branch condition keccak256(number) == secretNumberHash in guess().
A successful guess() execution reaches the external msg.sender.transfer(...) call before state is updated.
msg.sender is the untrusted recipient of the jackpot transfer, enabling reentrancy/callback on payment.
guess() computes this.balance + msg.value when building the payout amount.
The computed sum this.balance + msg.value is passed as the value of the external msg.sender.transfer call.

normalization_plan.reason: The uint8 parameter number is only used inside guess() to derive the hash comparison, so it normalizes into the guess function node.
